text.p: Leading stories in the Greek press:
ELEFTHEROTYPIA

--The Simitis government puts the emphasis on development, administration and social policy. Three 'super-ministries (interior, economy and development) Tsohatzopoulos an honourable move to defence. Arsenis swallows the 'sweet' pill and goes to education.
--Rift averted: Simitis mediates to get George Papandreou to accept deputy foreign ministry post.

--Former New Democracy president Miltiades Evert and former prime minister Constantine Mitsotakis set to battle it out over the leadership of the main opposition party. Evert's reported collecting of support from MPs draws fire from Mitsotakis who says that if Evert runs, he'll have Mitsotakis to deal with.
--Former conservative education minister George Souflias to announce today whether he will stand for ND president. Two others still considering.
--Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos in New York rejects Athens-Ankara dialogue over Cyprus as "inconceivable". Ankara should talk to Nicosia, he says.
ETHNOS
--Mitsotakis and Evert face off as the clouds of disunity gather over New Democracy. If Evert contests the leadership, so will I, Mitsotakis reported to have said.
--Simitis recipe for a government of cooperation and hope.
TA NEA
--Super-ministers in administration, economy and development in new, slightly bigger cabinet. Modernisers reign while 14 first-timers join the government.
--George Papandreou goes from no to yes in six hours of negotiations, following his initial refusal to accept deputy foreign ministry post.
ELEFTHEROS TYPOS
--Who's looking to keep Evert as New Democracy president. MPs gather signatures. Deputy president Ioannis Varvitsiotis - a possible contender for president - led by the need to keep the party united.
KATHIMERINI

--Yannos Papandoniou an economic 'czar', taking on finance as well as national economy portfolios in Prime Minister Costas Simitis's handpicked cabinet. Alekos Papadopoulos takes over at interior ministry.

--Simitis gets a bucketing from George Papandreou, who reluctantly lets go of the education portfolio to go to the alternate foreign ministry position. Gerasimos Arsenis takes over at education by requesting an "explanatory" announcement before leaving the defence ministry to Akis Tsohatzopoulos.
--New government expected to take speedy decisions, particularly in restructuring of public sector, reform of public finances and stepping up growth process.

--Changes in economic ministries welcomed by money markets. Papandoniou at head of ecofin ministries bodes well for development of capital market, while Papadopoulos at interior is a guarantee that public administration will be modernised and wasteful spending restricted.
--Simitis forming a special team of economic experts to study long-term macro-economic development problems affecting the Greek economy.
--Telecoms organisation (OTE) presents its profile to foreign institutional investors in London, New York and Boston next week. OTE has plans to offer up to 25 percent of shares to foreign investors.
IMERISIA

--Papandoniou at the wheel at the economic super-ministry a message to markets that economic policies will not change and that conflicts and 'malfunctions' between economy and finance ministries are at an end.

--New finance undersecretary Nikos Christodoulakis says ministry's first five measures will be of "strong social character", including farmers' pension fund, promoting major public works and measures to combat unemployment.
--Major foreign finance house buys out 11 percent of Aspis Pronia.
KERDOS
--One man rules economic policy: Yannos Papandoniou gets finance ministry as well.
--The drafting of the new budget a priority for the economic ministries. New budget is expected to give the flavour of intentions of the government's policies in 1997.
--Forex inflows to Greek market strengthens drachma slightly against the Ecu.
EXPRESS
--A continuation of economic policy: Papandoniou's appointment to both economy and finance aims at the more effective cooperation and better coordination between the two ministries.
--Asteras and National Insurance to merge. New state colossus in insurance market to play major role in Greek and Balkan markets.

--Federation of Greek Industries (SEB) calls for "a realistic economic policy". A strong electoral win and the four-year term ahead of Simitis's government creates the best conditions for the implementation of a programme with political boldness and realism, SEB says.
--Money markets breathe optimism, following announcement of new cabinet.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--Changes to government indicate a turn to fiscal policies. Papandoniou's appointment to both economy portfolios indicates the continuation of the government's economic policies.
--Finance ministry plans to take out new seven-year bond loan worth 800 billion drachmas from five Greek banks, reports say.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 331812-4
